fields.meta_description: Create a matrix survey question with one shared answer scale, one row per screen on phones, and an average for each row on a dashboard.
fields.h1: Build a Matrix Survey Question With Results for Every Row
fields.hero_description: Build a matrix survey question that rates several items on one scale and saves each row's answer to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Matrix Question
fields.features_subheading: A matrix asks several questions on one scale. Emergent builds the grid people answer and the table that keeps a score for each row.
fields.feature_1:
Rows and a scale from one prompt

Name the items and the scale, such as five statements on a 5-point agree scale. Emergent builds the grid, and a later prompt adds a row or renames a column label.
fields.feature_2:
One row per screen on a phone

On a phone, respondents see one row at a time with the scale as large buttons, and nobody scrolls sideways. A laptop shows the full grid with the same rows and labels.
fields.feature_3:
Each row saved as its own value

The answer to every row lands in its own column of a database you own, with the label chosen and its number on the scale. Put this round's rows beside the last round's.
fields.feature_4:
Per-row averages and an alert

The dashboard shows the average and the share who agree for each row. Set a floor for any row, and the app sends an email or a Slack message when its average drops under it.
fields.feature_5:
Same-column answers flagged

Ask the app to flag any response that picks the same column in every row. The dashboard shows each row with and without those answers, and you decide whether they count.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can export

Each matrix survey Emergent builds is code. On paid plans, export it to your GitHub repository with the rows, the scale and the dashboard, and run the next round from your repo.

plan.angle: The top 10 is help docs and explainers that define the grid, list types and repeat the same tips. None shows a finished matrix survey question with its results. This page shows the build and the readout together: rows and a shared scale set by prompt, one row per screen on a phone, per-row averages on a dashboard, a weekly alert when one row slips, answers that pick the same column in every row flagged, and every answer kept in a database the team owns. The FAQ covers what a builder decides before launch: size of the grid, phones, straight-lining, analysis and when not to use a grid.
tab_stories: Corriebrook Outfitters asks its 240 store staff to rate five statements on a 5-point agree scale; 212 answer, and the tools statement reaches 44% agreement while the other four reach 70% or more.

Saltmarsh Inn asks guests to rate four parts of their stay on a 5-point satisfaction scale; when a row's weekly average falls below 3.5 the general manager gets an email, and breakfast at 3.2 from 86 guests sent it this week.

Notewell, a note-taking app, asks 640 users how often they use five features on a Never to Always scale; 58 answers pick the same column in all five rows and are flagged, and in the other 582 export reaches 9% for Often or Always.
The Ashby Hollow parks board asks 1,130 residents on their phones to rate five park projects for importance, one row per screen; new restrooms average 4.4 out of 5 and go first in the spending plan.
